answer_summary: The dependency synchronization workflow (.github/workflows/gemini-supervisor-dependency-sync.yml) is a dedicated machine-maintenance system strictly separated from user-facing conversational runtime execution (.github/workflows/gemini-chat.yml). Triggered exclusively by push commits on main that modify either ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/Agents.md or send-to-gemini.js, it enforces a single-file base change constraint, evaluates mapped dependents via ChatMachines/GeminiEvaluation using an external LLM alignment prompt, and writes replacement files with a two-phase sentinel toggling mechanism to prevent recursive CI loops. The dependency map (dependency-map.json) maintains bidirectional mappings between Agents.md and send-to-gemini.js, designating config.json as an aligned dependent and tests/step-3-evaluation.json as read-only context. Orchestration evolved historically from an Apps Script message-stream echoer to an Apps Script transport layer, then to a direct GitHub Actions Node runner persisting run-scoped state, and finally separating maintenance automation from execution.

historical_facts.statement: Workflow gemini-supervisor-dependency-sync.yml triggers on pushes to main modifying either ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/Agents.md or ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/send-to-gemini.js, with concurrency group gemini-supervisor-dependency-sync and cancel-in-progress set to false.

The workflow checks ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/dependency-sync-sentinel.json; if enabled is false, it skips execution. It verifies git diff against BEFORE/SHA and throws a fatal error if COUNT of changed trigger files is not exactly 1.

The workflow dynamically configures ChatMachines/GeminiEvaluation/config.json with evaluation_mode 'generic', passes the authoritative base, mapped dependents, and read-only context files into generic_inputs, runs node evaluate-supervisor.js, and validates the response schema before writing file replacements.

When applying updates, the workflow first stages changes with sentinel enabled=false in commit 'Align GeminiSupervisor dependencies to <BASE>', pushes to main, and then commits enabled=true in commit 'Restore GeminiSupervisor dependency sync sentinel'.

dependency-map.json configures sentinel_file 'ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/dependency-sync-sentinel.json' and mappings for ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/Agents.md (dependents: send-to-gemini.js, config.json; context: tests/step-3-evaluation.json) and send-to-gemini.js (dependents: Agents.md, config.json; context: tests/step-3-evaluation.json).

gemini-chat.yml originated on 2026-09-29 as GeminiChatGPTAppScript/send-to-gemini.js appending to MessageStream/messages.json, was renamed to GeminiSupervisor, moved nextmessage to nextmessage/nextmessage.json, migrated to an Apps Script web app endpoint, pivoted on 2026-09-30 to direct GitHub Actions Node execution with run-scoped directory persistence, briefly branched for gemini-edit-agents.js, and added step gate metadata checkpoint commit messages.
dependency-map.json and gemini-supervisor-dependency-sync.yml were committed on 2026-10-01 (commits b899191 and 7839cfd), following the creation of supervisor config.json (commit 7cf2f4c).

interpretations.statement: The repository enforces an architectural separation between user-facing runtime execution (gemini-chat.yml, triggered by nextmessage/nextmessage.json) and peer artifact synchronization (gemini-supervisor-dependency-sync.yml, triggered by specification/code modifications). Maintenance operations do not run during conversational turn execution.

dependency-map.json accurately reflects active supervisor dependencies (Agents.md, send-to-gemini.js, config.json, and tests/step-3-evaluation.json) without obsolete paths. However, it establishes an asymmetric alignment architecture: while Agents.md and send-to-gemini.js act as bidirectional authoritative bases that update config.json, config.json and tests/step-3-evaluation.json are neither triggers nor authoritative bases, meaning changes originating directly in those files do not trigger automated synchronization.

The two-step sentinel toggle (setting enabled: false in the alignment commit and enabled: true in a secondary restoration commit) combined with the single-base diff constraint deterministically prevents infinite workflow re-triggering loops when GitHub Actions commits modifications back to main.

truth_decisions.statement: The dependency synchronization workflow operates deterministically via strict trigger path filters, single-base validation, isolated evaluator execution, and sentinel suppression.

dependency-map.json accurately maps repository paths without obsolete linkages, though peer artifacts config.json and step-3-evaluation.json are strictly reactive dependents or read-only context rather than base triggers.

unresolved_questions: Whether direct manual edits to config.json or tests/step-3-evaluation.json have occurred without a corresponding trigger run on Agents.md or send-to-gemini.js cannot be determined from workflow definitions alone without complete repository commit logs.
